Elevated panoramic view eastward from the western hills across the Tiber into ancient Rome in September AD96. Reference is style-only; do not include its people.

Inside Domitian's imperial palace on the Palatine, discreet household messengers carry sealed folded communications and small wax tablets between private apartments. Wide corridor with polished variegated marble columns, red-and-ochre painted walls, geometric marble floor and dark timber apartment doors. One adult messenger quietly hands a sealed folded note to another at a doorway, a third servant walks deeper into the residence carrying a tablet. Quiet purposeful domestic service, natural gestures and subdued expressions, no overt melodramatic conspiracy. Afternoon courtyard light. Reference is architectural/style reference only; Domitian himself need not appear.

Dramatic historical illustration of the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on Rome's Capitoline hill during a thunderstorm, under Domitian before his death in AD96. Three-quarter architectural view from the sacred forecourt. Reconstruct the Domitianic temple as a broad nearly square Roman temple on a high podium with a deep front portico of SIX white marble Corinthian columns across its facade, wide stone stairway, triangular sculpted pediment, three cella entrances recessed behind the portico, gilded roof tiles and roof statuary. One vivid branching lightning bolt strikes the temple's upper roof, momentarily illuminating marble and rain. Dark storm clouds, wind-driven rain and reflections on stone paving, distant low first-century rooftops. Temple still standing, not exploding, no invented collapse or massive fire. Imposing atmospheric painting. Reference style only, no emperor in scene.

Purposeful urgent expressions and restrained postures, a short dagger lowered discreetly at one entrant's side but no attack shown. Domitian's recognisable pale closed-eyed face is still visible at the head while cloth is being folded over his fully covered torso and legs. Phyllis stands near his head watching solemnly, one hand resting lightly on the bier edge. No wounds, blood, decay or nudity. Plain plaster walls, wooden door, terracotta vessels, soft indirect daylight and deep shade; humble, compassionate preparation, not a grand imperial funeral or a modern embalming room. Maintain distinct face of Phyllis; attendants are anonymous.

entries.title: Phyllis places Domitians ashes beside Julias
entries.text:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: VENIVIDIVICI illustrated historical film still. ONE separate full-frame landscape 16:9 image. Never a collage or multiple panels. Match established references exactly in refined painterly historical reconstruction style: naturalistic painted faces, classical history painting detail, warm ochre, red, ivory and bronze, believable Roman surfaces and clothing, cinematic yet restrained light, no photographic or glossy 3D look. AD96, imperial Rome. No text, labels, lettering, logos, watermarks, signatures or corner emblems. References are identity/style sources, not a composition to copy. Violence is restrained, non-graphic historical drama: no exposed organs, open wounds, severed parts, blood spray, pools of blood or gore.
Phyllis MUST be the identical elderly woman from her reference: long lined face, sun-weathered olive complexion, strong slightly hooked nose, grey-brown hair centre parted and gathered into a low loose bun, concerned deep-set eyes. Plain ivory tunic and worn indigo-blue wool mantle, modest and dignified, no jewellery or imperial finery. Inside a quiet funerary chamber associated with Rome's Temple of the Flavian family, Phyllis carefully sets a small plain lidded terracotta urn holding Domitian's cremated remains next to an older slightly larger pale stone funerary urn holding Julia's remains on a low marble shelf. Both vessels clearly visible close together, her hands respectfully lowering the smaller urn. This is a discreet intimate moment, no living woman Julia in the scene, no modern cemetery, cross, portraits, inscriptions or readable labels. Restrained Roman carved stone niches and painted plaster, one bronze oil lamp illuminates her face and the two urns, soft ambient light from a high opening. Compassionate solemn mood; not a lavish public ceremony. Exact arrangement is illustrative, not an archaeological facsimile.

entries.title: Visual art style and animation
entries.text:
## VISUAL ART STYLE AND ANIMATION — VENIVIDIVICI

All episode imagery must follow a consistent illustrated historical-art aesthetic rather than resembling photorealistic film footage.

**Visual style:**
- Inspired by classical historical paintings, Roman frescoes, mosaics and archaeological reconstruction illustrations.
- Painterly, atmospheric, detailed and historically grounded.
- Rich textures resembling traditional painting, with natural brushwork and subtle artistic imperfections.
- Warm Mediterranean colours: ochre, terracotta, marble white, muted gold, dusty red, earthy greens and soft blues.
- Historically accurate Roman architecture, clothing, hairstyles, furnishings, weapons and everyday objects appropriate to the period.
- Compositions should resemble sophisticated historical illustrations or museum-quality paintings rather than Hollywood film stills.
- Images may vary between classical painting, fresco-inspired artwork and detailed illustrated reconstructions while maintaining a unified visual identity.
- Avoid glossy CGI, hyperrealistic photography, modern cinematic lens effects, cartoon aesthetics and fantasy imagery.

**Animation and movement:**
- Primarily use illustrated still images with gentle movement added during editing.
- Slow pans, gradual zooms, subtle parallax and soft dissolves create the impression of moving through a historical painting.
- Where appropriate, restrained environmental animation may include flickering flames, flowing water, drifting smoke, moving clouds or gently shifting fabric.
- Avoid exaggerated character movement, artificial facial animation, dramatic camera movements or distracting visual effects.
- Preserve the original painterly appearance when animating images. Animation must never transform the artwork into photorealistic video.
- Visual transitions should support the pace and atmosphere of the narration without drawing attention away from the story.

**Technical requirements:**
- Landscape 16:9 composition, preferably 1920 × 1080 or higher.
- No embedded text, subtitles, watermarks or modern objects.
- Maintain consistent appearances for recurring historical figures and fictional characters.
- Images should accompany and enhance the narration, not attempt to illustrate every spoken sentence literally.

**Overall objective:** The viewer should feel as though they are being guided through a beautifully illustrated history book, with paintings and reconstructions gently coming to life as the story unfolds.
